theory.intro: Worded problems here use halves, thirds, quarters, fifths and tenths of money, length, mass or a group. Find the fraction by dividing by the denominator and multiplying by the numerator, or by multiplying first and then dividing.
facts: Read the question to see whether it wants the part **taken**, or the part **left over**.
Divide first if the quotient will be a whole number; otherwise, multiplying first can be easier. Keep exact values without rounding, using fractions or exact decimals as appropriate.
steps: Identify the quantity and the fraction.
Divide by the denominator and multiply by the numerator, choosing which to do first. Divide first if it gives a whole number; otherwise, multiplying first can be easier.
Answer the actual question — sometimes you must subtract from the whole.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) One quarter is $36\div4=9$ students.
Three quarters is $9\times3=27$ students.
(b) $36-27=9$ students do not bring lunch.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A shop reduces a $\$26$ item by one quarter of its price. Find the sale price.
(b) A container has capacity $11$ litres and is three fifths full. How much water does it contain?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The discount is $\$26\div4=\$6.50$.
$\$26-\$6.50=\$19.50$.
The sale price is $\$19.50$.
(b) One fifth is $11\div5=2.2$ litres.
Three fifths is $2.2\times3=6.6$ litres.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A tank of capacity $320$ litres is three quarters full. Two fifths of the water is used. How much remains?
(b) Four tenths of $95$ tickets are sold on Monday.
How many tickets is this?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) One quarter is $320\div4=80$ litres.
Three quarters is $80\times3=240$ litres.
One fifth of the water is $240\div5=48$ litres.
Two fifths is $48\times2=96$ litres used.
$240-96=144$ litres remain.
(b) One tenth is $95\div10=9.5$ tickets.
Four tenths is $9.5\times4=38$ tickets.

foundation.question_text:
A class has $30$ students.
$\frac{2}{5}$ bring lunch.
How many students bring lunch?

A $40$ m rope has $\frac{3}{4}$ used.
How many metres are used?

Kai spends $\frac{2}{10}$ of $\$70$.
How much does he spend?

A basket holds $45$ oranges.
$\frac{3}{5}$ are sold.
How many remain?

A bag holds $28$ kg when full.
$\frac{1}{4}$ of its contents has been removed from the full bag.
How many kilograms are in the bag?
foundation.solution_text:
$28\div4=7$ kg removed
$28-7=21$ kg in the bag

foundation.question_text:
Mia reads $\frac{7}{10}$ of a $120$-page book.
How many pages does she read?

development.question_text:
A runner completes $\frac{3}{4}$ of a $64$ km relay route.
How far remains?

A shop discounts a $\$90$ bag by $\frac{1}{4}$ of its price.
What is the sale price?

A recipe uses $\frac{3}{5}$ of a $750$ g packet.
How many grams remain?

A school plants $\frac{4}{10}$ of $235$ trees on Monday.
How many trees is this?

A $9$ L container is filled to $\frac{3}{4}$ of capacity.
How many litres does it contain?

Noah spends $\frac{3}{5}$ of $\$175$ on a game.
How much does he spend?

mastery.question_text:
A tank contains $\frac{7}{10}$ of its $350$ L capacity.
Then $\frac{2}{5}$ of the water is used.
How much water remains?

A $\$240$ budget spends $\frac{3}{4}$ on food and $\frac{2}{5}$ of the remainder on transport.
How much remains?

A library lends $\frac{3}{5}$ of $420$ books.
Of those, $\frac{1}{4}$ are returned.
How many are still on loan?
mastery.solution_text:
$420\div5\times3=252$ lent
$252\div4=63$ returned
$252-63=189$ books still on loan
